lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northside Bakery | Delivery Driver | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Delivered morning wholesale orders to about 20 cafés and collected signed invoices.
- Loaded the van and checked each order against the dispatch list before leaving.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Owned the end-of-line test station for the humidity sensor and the yield reports the line leads used.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Built a solar-powered weather station on an STM32 that reports every 5 minutes over LoRa and runs 9 days without sun.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- Wrote the CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard and tested it against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, osciloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The engineering experience is not ordered newest first.
items.because: Clearwater Sensors appears above the more recent Voltline Robotics role.

items.says: The Northside Bakery entry should be shortened to a single line.
items.because: Its two bullets take space from engineering experience and projects.

items.says: The review says “cafØs” is corrupted spelling.
items.because: It may look like a typo or encoding error.

items.says: The delivery duties have no stated result or value.
The dispatch-list check has no stated result.
“Before leaving” repeats the pre-departure timing conveyed by the check.
The line does not say what changed as a result of the yield reports.
“Owned” describes responsibility rather than a specific action.
The quantified return reduction appears at the end instead of leading the line.
The test-fixture line is a stronger opening line for the entry.
The 60% update-speed improvement has no comparison baseline.
items.because: Without a prior duration or other reference point, its size is hard to judge.

items.says: The test count shows the rig’s scope but not its effect.
The five-failure diagnosis is buried after the logger’s implementation details.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: An 8 kHz sample rate has a 4 kHz Nyquist frequency, below the signal’s frequency.

items.says: Declaring the counter volatile does not, by itself, fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make accesses atomic or synchronize the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: The phrase about the counter shared by the interrupt handler and main loop repeats context.
items.because: It lengthens the sentence without clarifying the race condition.

items.says: The line does not say what changed in the program’s behavior.
The quantified outcomes are delayed by the fleet scope, and this is the stronger opening line for the entry.
The nine-day runtime lacks battery capacity or test-setup context.
items.because: Runtime depends on stored energy and operating conditions.

items.says: The current-reduction line is the strongest line in the project entry and should lead it.
“Openly” is vague and may repeat what “Published” conveys.
The bullet attributes robot-fleet motor-controller work to a Formula Student electric-car project.
items.because: The project context conflicts with the warehouse robot-fleet work described under Voltline.

items.says: The CAN-dashboard line does not say what the testing established or changed.
The CAN-dashboard line is the stronger opening line for the entry.
“Before each race” emphasizes timing rather than the testing’s value.
The fleet and motor-control results duplicate the Voltline achievement and are attributed to Formula Student.
items.because: The student project ended before the Voltline role began, and Voltline states matching results.

items.says: “osciloscopes” is misspelled in the Tools line.
items.because: The conspicuous misspelling obscures the intended tool name and can look unproofread.
